papers.title: Effect of scanning pattern and volumetric energy density on the properties of selective laser melting Ti-6Al-4V specimens
papers.abstract: Selective laser melting (SLM) is a potential additive manufacturing method for fabricating Ti-6Al-4V parts; however, the shortage of practical knowledge about the effect of volumetric energy density (VED) and scan pattern on the quality and defect formation of SLMed Ti-6Al-4V parts limited its use. In this paper, attempts are made to address the effect of some of the key process parameters on the location and type of defects, mass density, and hardness of the Ti-6Al-4V specimens manufactured via the SLM process. It was found that selecting proper VED cannot fully guarantee to reach a high-density part (>99%), and both scan pattern and VED must be considered as a combination for fabricating a high-density product. Moreover, the results of this study showed that the scan pattern plays a vital role in the defect type and its location. Thus, to produce a quality part, the selected scan pattern must be in accordance with the applied VED. The hardness of the specimens was evaluated and related to the applied scan pattern and resulting mass density. The hardness of high-density specimens at side surfaces were near to that of the wrought material, while at the top surfaces the hardness could be 10% higher than the wrought Ti-6Al-4V material.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了SLM Ti-6Al-4V的扫描模式和能量密度对密度和硬度的影响，未涉及多孔结构、应力遮挡或疲劳性能。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address porous structure design, stress shielding, fatigue testing, or surface roughness relevant to osseointegration, which are core to the AM biomedical materials direction.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究扫描模式和体积能量密度对SLM Ti-6Al-4V质量的影响。
summary_zh.method: 改变工艺参数制造Ti-6Al-4V试样，测试密度、缺陷和硬度。
summary_zh.result: 体积能量密度和扫描模式共同决定致密度和缺陷位置，硬度与锻造材料相当。
summary_zh.validation: 通过密度测量和硬度测试验证工艺参数的影响。

summary_en.motivation: To understand how scanning pattern and volumetric energy density affect the quality and defect formation in selective laser melted Ti-6Al-4V parts.
summary_en.method: Ti-6Al-4V specimens were fabricated with varying volumetric energy densities and scanning patterns, then characterized for mass density, defect type and location, and hardness.
summary_en.result: Both volumetric energy density and scanning pattern significantly influence density and defect distribution; high-density specimens exhibit hardness comparable to wrought material.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through density measurements and hardness testing, demonstrating the combined effect of the two process parameters.
